title: Abdominal Pain
correct_orders: Perform physical examination with focus on abdominal examination
Order complete blood count (CBC), basic metabolic panel, lipase, amylase
Consider imaging studies such as ultrasound or CT scan of the abdomen
Consult general surgery if signs of surgical emergency (e.g., peritonitis, rebound tenderness)
Initiate broad-spectrum antibiotics for suspected intra-abdominal infection
Order: Order: time-sensitive interventions first; (oxygen, IV access, glucose check)

rationale.Obtain vital signs: To assess the patient's overall condition
rationale.Perform physical examination with focus: To identify potential localizing signs for abdominal pain
rationale.Order complete blood count (CBC), basic: For general diagnostic workup of acute abdomen
rationale.Consider imaging studies such as ultraso: To help determine the cause of the abdominal pain and identify any potential complications
rationale.Consult general surgery if signs of surg: For management of potential surgical emergencies
rationale.Initiate broad-spectrum antibiotics for: To cover common abdominal pathogens while waiting for culture results
rationale.Consider pain management as needed: For comfort and to help manage the patient's symptoms
rationale.Oxygen: Abdominal pain could be indicative of a variety of conditions, some potentially life-threatening. Oxygen is a necessary first step to ensure adequate oxygenation and stabilization.
rationale.Order: Order: time-sensitive interventio: IV access is crucial for administering fluids, medications, and blood products if needed. A glucose check can help rule out diabetes as a potential cause of the abdominal pain.

hpi:
Initial History

Reason(s) for visit: Abdominal Pain
History of present Illness:
A 22-year-old female presents to the emergency room with abdominal pain, lethargy, and vomiting x2 days. Her vomiting is non-bloody. Her abdominal pain is diffuse, which she rates as a 6/10. She also claims to have had an increased appetite prior to having these symptoms. She also claims that she’s been developing blurry vision, dizziness, and drowsiness. She also states that she is having increased urination

Past Medical History

Past Medical History: None
Current medications: Birth control
Allergies: None
Vaccinations: The patient received her childhood vaccinations. She has never received any HPV vaccines.
Women's health: The patient cannot remember when her last pap smear was done.
Family History: The patient has a brother with Diabetes. 

Social History:
Marital/Family: Single. She is an undergraduate student at a local university.
Personal habits: The patient denies smoking. She drinks socially. She smoked marijuana "a few times" with her friends. She denies other illicit drugs or misuse of medications. Occupation/educational: She is a student at a local university
Recreational: She plays the piano and sings in a band. 

Review of systems:
General: See HPI
Skin: Her skin is dry. 
HEENT: Her throat is dry. 
Cardiorespiratory: She feels that her heart is beating faster.
Gastrointestinal: See HPI
Genitourinary: See HPI
Neuropsychiatric: See HPI
